summary.title: LLaTiSA: Towards Difficulty-Stratified Time Series Reasoning from Visual Perception to Semantics

setting_and_object.category: Dataset + Algorithm (hierarchical time-series-reasoning dataset and a VLM-based reasoning model)

details: Time series reasoning (TSR) research is fragmented: heterogeneous task definitions and benchmarks with ambiguous labels/insufficient context, and no test of basic numerical read-out.
Vision-centric VLM approaches capture shapes but lack precise value grounding, while text/TS-encoder approaches fail on pattern perception.

A four-level difficulty-stratified TSR taxonomy (L1 numerical read-out, L2 pattern perception, L3 semantic reasoning, L4 predictive inference) instantiated as HiTSR, an 83k-sample dataset with unambiguous ground truth and verified chain-of-thought trajectories.

LLaTiSA: a VLM-based TSR model whose defining mechanism is dual-view visual input, pairing the standard series plot with a second image that renders the series as a precision-calibrated index-value numeric table, trained by a curriculum of stage-wise SFT following the L1→L2→L3 hierarchy.
HiTSR-L1 (30,000 samples, synthetic series from ChatTS pipeline, rule-generated short-answer tasks: min/max grounding, multi-series comparison, start/end comparison, subseries localization).
HiTSR-L2 (50,703 samples, synthetic; local/global pattern differentiation and numerical perception as multiple choice, distractors from perturbations or other series).
HiTSR-L3 (3,121 samples) built from real-world corpora (ETT, Weather, Traffic, UTSD, Monash, Time-MMD) with metadata-grounded MCQs generated by GPT-5.
CoT annotation by GPT-5 with cross-validation; 10% held-out human-audited test sets (L3 fully human-verified); cross-model check with Qwen3-235B gives average Cohen's kappa 0.848.
Backbone Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct; three-stage SFT (27k L1 samples 1 epoch, 45k L2 2 epochs, 2.7k L3 2 epochs), lr 1e-5, AdamW, 8xH20 GPUs.
Optional fourth-stage domain SFT: 30k ECG-Grounding samples, or (appendix) 4,993 L4 successor-selection items with L4 rendered as a 2x2 grid of candidate plots plus numeric table.
L1: real-world subset of HiTSR-L1 (model trained only on synthetic); L2: 500 sampled BEDTime items (local) and MMTS-Bench subset (120, global); L3: 100 sampled MCQ2 items.
Domain transfer: ECG-Grounding ID/OOD with metrics for diagnosis accuracy, lead assessment coverage/accuracy, evidence-based reasoning.
Metrics: accuracy, half-accuracy (locating one of max/min), and success rate for valid answer generation.
Encoding-strategy sweep under the same backbone/training: text with and without indices, single plot image, single numeric-table image, plot+text dual modality.
Off-the-shelf models: GPT-4o (as LLM and VLM), Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-VL-8B, InternVL3-8B, Gemma3-12B; TSRMs Time-R1, Time-MQA, ChatTime; TS-MLLMs ChatTS, OpenTSLM; ECG-specific GEM (LLaVA/PULSE) and PULSE.
No-CoT SFT (correct option only) vs CoT supervision.
Single-stage joint training (shuffled pooled levels) vs sequential curriculum; single-level-only training (only L1, only L2) and partial curricula.
Appendix L4 curriculum extension (L1→L2→L3 vs L1→L2→L3→L4 vs L1+L2+L3+L4 joint).

key_findings.finding: Pairing a series plot with an image of the numeric index-value table gives a VLM both pattern perception and precise numerical grounding, outperforming all other encoding strategies and much larger proprietary models on OOD TSR.
key_findings.evidence: On OOD L1 min/max localization LLaTiSA reaches 86.8% accuracy versus 54.2% for the best baseline (GPT-4o with vision+indexed text) and 2.4% for GPT-4o with plot+numeric-table images; L2 local 75.6% vs 72.2% (GPT-4o vision), L2 global 97.5%, L3 67.0% vs 59.0% (ChatTS). Under matched backbone/training, single-plot input scores 68.0% L2-local but cannot do L1, while single numeric-table input scores 86.8% L1 but only 32.4% L2-local; the dual view attains the best of both.

key_findings.finding: Existing LLMs, VLMs and specialized TSR models essentially fail foundational point-level numerical read-out, revealing a perception-reasoning gap that motivates the L1 diagnostic level.
key_findings.evidence: OOD L1 accuracy is 0.0% for Time-R1 and Time-MQA, 7.8% for ChatTS, 2.0-2.4% for VLMs given plot+table images, and 47.4% for GPT-4o on raw text; ChatTime scores 0.0%. Text-based models often loop repetitively and exceed context length (success rates 17.4-68%). On HiTSR, adding time indices to textual arrays lifts GPT-4o L1 from 6.0% to 23.0%.

key_findings.finding: Sequential curriculum fine-tuning along the taxonomy is necessary; joint or single-level training degrades generalization, particularly on higher-level semantic reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: Joint training loses 1.74% (L2) and 14.93% (L3) relative accuracy OOD versus the curriculum (L3 OOD 57.0 vs 67.0); training on L2 alone collapses L1 to 10.0% OOD, showing high-level skills do not back-propagate to grounding; in the L4 extension the curriculum reaches 83.3% versus 75.4% for joint L1+L2+L3+L4 and 54.2% without the L4 stage.

key_findings.finding: Verified CoT supervision, rather than answer-only labels, is what drives out-of-distribution transfer and preserves instruction-following.
key_findings.evidence: Removing CoT leaves ID performance nearly unchanged (L2 97.0, L3 80.0) but drops OOD accuracy by 4.31% on L2 and 17.91% on L3 (L3 OOD 55.0 vs 67.0), and the answer-only model no longer emits reasoning chains even when explicitly prompted.

key_findings.finding: HiTSR-pretrained LLaTiSA acts as a data-efficient foundation for domain-specific L3 reasoning such as grounded ECG interpretation.
key_findings.evidence: Fine-tuned on 30k ECG-Grounding samples (2.5% of GEM's 1.186M instructions), it beats GEM (LLaVA) by 18.14% lead assessment coverage and 14.22% lead accuracy ID and exceeds an identically fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B on all metrics (+5.42% diagnosis accuracy, +4.39% evidence-based reasoning OOD), though it trails GEM on overall diagnosis accuracy (62.8 vs 87.2 ID).
